newsitem.title: USA: NFL-SEAHAWKS UPSET DOLPHINS, VIKINGS AND PACKERS WIN.
newsitem.headline: NFL-SEAHAWKS UPSET DOLPHINS, VIKINGS AND PACKERS WIN.

text.p: John Friesz, making his first start of the season, threw three long touchdown passes -- including an 80-yarder to Brian Blades with 2:03 to go -- as the Seattle Seahawks stunned the Miami Dolphins 22-15 Sunday.

Friesz, who replaced slumping Rick Mirer at quarterback, was 18-of-32 for 301 yards. He threw a pair of touchdown passes to Joey Galloway three minutes apart in the first half and atoned for his only interception with the pass to Blades, a native of Miami.
The Dolphins (3-2) played without star quarterback Dan Marino -- out with a broken ankle -- and lost their second consecutive game.

In Baltimore, Drew Bledsoe passed for 310 yards and four touchdowns as the New England Patriots held off a furious fourth quarter comeback by the Baltimore Ravens to win their third straight game 46-38.

New England (3-2) exploded for 32 points in the middle quarters, paced by Bledsoe, who went 12-of-13 for 149 yards and two touchdowns in the third quarter. The Patriots scored on five straight possesions to take a seemingly comfortable lead in the third quarter.
Bledsoe completed 25-of-39 passes with no interceptions and went over the 1,000 yard mark in passing this season with 1,217 yards.

In Chicago, Brett Favre passed for four touchdowns, including a pair to Antonio Freeman, for the second straight week and Don Beebe returned a kickoff 90 yards for a score to lead the Green Bay Packers to a 37-6 rout of the Chicago Bears.
Favre hit Robert Brooks with an 18-yard scoring pass in the first quarter and passed for two more touchdowns in the final 35 seconds of the second quarter to give the Packers a 20-3 halftime lead.
Favre has passed for 20 touchdowns in six games this season and recorded his seventh career four-touchdown game.

In Detroit, Scott Mitchell threw three touchdown passes and ran for another as the Detroit Lions survived three rushing touchdowns by Jamal Anderson to post a 28-24 victory over the winless Atlanta Falcons.

Mitchell scored on a two-yard run 7:56 into the game and added a nine-yard touchdown pass to Brett Perriman and a pair of scoring strikes to Herman Moore in the second quarter to stake the Lions to a 28-0 lead.

But Anderson scored from nine yards out seven seconds before halftime and had TD runs of five and 14 yards in the third period to close the gap to 28-21. Morten Andersen contributed a 47-yard field goal with 5:57 remaining to cut the deficit to four points.
But the Lions went on a 78-yard drive to the Falcon 1 and kneeled on the ball rather than punch it in.
At Minnesota, Warren Moon hooked up with Cris Carter for a pair of touchdowns and the Minnesota Vikings forced six Carolina turnovers, including four interceptions, to defeat the Panthers 14-12.
The win kept the Vikings (5-1) tied with Green Bay for first-place in the NFC Central.
Moon completed 19-of-34 passes for 209 yards and moved ahead of Dan Fouts into third-place on the all-time pass yardage list with 43,105 yards.
Carter had seven catches for 90 yards to become only the 14th player in NFL history to have 600 career receptions.
In East Rutherford, New Jersey, the Jets crashed again, losing 34-13 to the Oakland Radiers.
Jeff Hostetler threw three touchdown passes -- two to rookie tight end Rickey Dudley -- and Joe Aska rushed for a career-high 136 yards for Oakland.
The Raiders (2-4) held the Jets to a pair of Nick Lowery field goals before rookie Alex Van Dyke's three-yard touchdown reception with 3:48 remaining.

The miserable Jets have lost their first six games this season and 19 of 22 games since the 1995 season. The Jets also lost starting quarterback Neil O'Donnell for four-to-six weeks with a separated right shoulder.
